criteria.evidence: All five guided sections plus Agent intent (ICE) are substantive: 'What it does' names when it runs ('a play is about to plan, break down or build from the ICE of a node'), what it reads and gives, and what it replaces; Inputs/Outputs names --done, --node, --out and exit codes 0/1/2; eight Given/When/Then criteria; Out of scope names fn-725, /discover-domains, cap-718 and bi-722.
'The two copies of the script stay the same: the reference copy in create-play and the copy in discover-intent. A play that works on ICE copies the reference with no change.'
criteria.fix: Add the why to this rule, e.g. 'so every play that checks readiness gives the same answer for the same model; if the copies drift, two plays could disagree on whether a node is ready.' The other rules already carry their reason (e.g. 'A met intent counts, because it was confirmed first', 'Thus a link to an intent that nobody wrote never makes a node ready').

criteria.evidence: Rules are one-point bullets; acceptance is strict Given/When/Then, e.g. 'Given a capability with an empty domain that serves a confirmed business intent and needs nothing, when the ready check runs on it, then it is ready (exit 0) and its warnings include "has no domain yet".' The function is stated as behavior, not a user story.

Parent line: 'Ready without a domain (fn-724): the ready check gives its answer without the domain.' Child adds the per-kind ready rules, missing-intent-page handling, the --done/--node inputs, the exit codes, the holding-folder case and the file-only determinism rule.

'"Ready" means a play can plan or build from the node. A capability is ready when it serves a confirmed business intent and nothing it needs is open... A missing domain is a warning, never a block.' plus 'What it replaces: the ADR 043 rule... That rule blocked a plan built directly from a business intent.' and an Out of scope list naming each neighbour. A cold reader can state the what, the why and the edges from this doc alone.
